description: We are nexTera, a passionate team of first-year B.Tech Food Technology students at Amal Jyothi College of Engineering. Combining food science, biotechnology, and data-driven innovation, we are building AstroPalate-a sensory-compensated nutrition and health- monitoring tool designed to combat microgravity flavor fatigue and nutrient loss for astronauts on deep-space missions. Driven by curiosity and real-world impact, we bring fresh biological perspectives to space exploration!
summary:
AstroPalate is a sensory-compensated health and nutrition monitoring platform designed to prevent microgravity-induced malnutrition and spaceflight anorexia during long-duration space missions.

In microgravity, upward fluid shifts cause chronic nasal congestion ("space sniffles"), suppressing olfaction—which drives nearly 80% of flavor perception. Combined with repetitive menus, this leads astronauts to consume 20–30% fewer calories than required, accelerating bone demineralization, muscle atrophy, and immune decline. Unlike passive calorie loggers, AstroPalate links a 10-second daily crew check-in (tracking sinus congestion, fatigue, hydration, circadian disruption, and radiation exposure) with Food Technology interventions. Its sensory engine recommends trigeminal stimulants (capsaicin, ginger, piperine) and umami-rich space rations to restore appetite without excess sodium, while prioritizing bone-protective micronutrients (Vitamin D3, calcium, potassium) and tracking shelf-life vitamin degradation (Vitamins B1, C, and K).

Powered by open NASA datasets—including Spaceflight Standard Measures, NASA OSDR/GeneLab, and the Human Research Program Evidence Book—AstroPalate requires zero extra hardware mass and transforms daily astronaut rations into precision preventive medicine for low-Earth orbit, lunar habitats, and Mars transit.
details:
AstroPalate is a sensory-compensated astronaut health and nutrition monitoring software designed to prevent microgravity-induced malnutrition and spaceflight anorexia during long-duration space missions. In microgravity, upward cephalic fluid shifts cause chronic nasal congestion ("space sniffles"), suppressing olfaction—which drives nearly 80% of human flavor perception. Combined with repetitive menus, astronauts often consume 20–30% fewer calories than required, accelerating bone demineralization, muscle atrophy, and immune decline.

AstroPalate replaces passive calorie logging with an active, four-stage Food Technology workflow:

  1. 10-Second Daily Cabin Check-In: Crew members log subjective symptoms (sinus congestion, taste fatigue, nausea, and stress on a 1–5 scale) alongside biometric telemetry (heart rate, sleep quality, hydration, and radiation exposure).
  2. Sensory-Compensation Engine: When nasal congestion is elevated, the software recommends space rations enriched with trigeminal stimulants (capsaicin, ginger, piperine, menthol) and umami compounds (glutamates, nucleotides) that stimulate oral nerve receptors directly—restoring appetite without adding excess sodium (which accelerates bone calcium loss in space).
  3. Micronutrient Bioavailability Matcher: Aligns meal selection with physiological deficits, prioritizing Vitamin D3, Calcium, Potassium, and Omega-3s to counter ~1–1.5% monthly microgravity bone loss, while scheduling tyrosine-rich daytime foods and melatonin-tart evening snacks to stabilize 90-minute orbital circadian cycles.
  4. Radiation Shelf-Life Guard & Flight Surgeon Sync: Tracks spacecraft ration inventory and prioritizes thermostabilized or rehydratable pouches before cosmic radiation degrades sensitive vitamins (Vitamins B1, C, and K), while exporting lightweight daily telemetry summaries for ground flight surgeons.

Benefits & Intended Impact

  • Prevents Spaceflight Anorexia: Projected to boost daily caloric compliance by up to +22%, protecting astronaut muscle mass, bone density, and cognitive performance on ISS, Lunar Gateway, and Mars transit missions.
  • Reduces Spacecraft Ration Waste: Cuts nutrient-degraded food waste by up to 35% through shelf-life prioritization.
  • Zero Additional Launch Mass: Runs natively on existing crew tablets and wearable telemetry feeds without adding hardware payload weight.
  • Earth Healthcare Spin-Off: Directly adaptable for chemotherapy patients, elderly care, and post-viral anosmia patients experiencing severe taste/smell loss.

Creativity & Key Factors Considered Most astronaut health tools (such as NASA's Food Intake Tracker and ESA's EveryWear) passively record macros or rely on delayed Earth-based dietitian reviews. AstroPalate is creative because it applies Food Technology and sensory biology to solve an aerospace medical bottleneck autonomously—making it essential for deep-space missions where Earth communication delays reach up to 20 minutes. Our team specifically accounted for sodium-induced hypercalciuria, radiation-driven vitamin decay kinetics, zero-gravity crumb/liquid packaging constraints, and low-friction usability for busy crew schedules.

Tools, Datasets & Software Used

  • Scientific & Data Benchmarks: NASA Spaceflight Standard Measures, NASA Open Science Data Repository (OSDR / GeneLab), NASA Human Research Program (HRP) Evidence Book, and NASA Space Food Systems Laboratory thermal-processing stability data.
  • Design, Prototyping & Documentation: Google Workspace (Docs, Slides, Drive), Canva / Adobe Express for crew tablet UI wireframes, and rule-based nutritional decision modeling.
